newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine airports sale seen advancing in Congress.
newsitem.headline: Argentine airports sale seen advancing in Congress.

text.p: An congressional committee has reached agreement on the sale of Argentina's 59 airports, the state news agency Telam reported Wednesday.

The modifications to the legislation after the Senate asked for change to the initial proposal paves the way for the passage of the privatization bill through the lower house of Congress before year's end.
"We agreed at the committee level and I will ask for the bill to be treated at the next session of Congress," said Jorge Telmo Perez, head of the airports committee, according to Telam.

The committee, made up of the heads of the lower house's transportation, defence and budget commissions, agreed to limit the compensation that current operators will receive on the various services up for tender.
In addition, the plan spells out that the airport concessions will be split up into various zones across the country. More than one operator will be chosen in each region.
Also, provincial governments and municipalities will be able to take part in the tenders alongside private operators.
The government had sent the privatization proposal to the Senate which made changes to the original. When deputies approves the new suggestions, the proposal wil be sent to the Senate again.
The proceeds from the privatization of the airports have been included in next year's budget so the speedy passage of the proposal will come as a relief to the government.

The concessions for the airports will be for 30 years and winners in the tenders will have to invest about $1.6 billion to bring the airports up to scratch. Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) is advising the government on the sale.
